newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close higher on weekly crush data.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close higher on weekly crush data.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures ended sharply higher on Friday, led by old crop July, on weekly crush figures that came in well above trade expectations, floor traders said.
The National Oilseed Processors Association put the crush figure for the week ended May 28 at 25.462 million bushels, above trade expectations for 23 million to 23.7 million.

"Thirty-one million bushels this week in crush and export is far too much to ensure we have sufficient ending stocks," said Joel Karlin, analyst with Everen Securities. "Even with these high prices there continues to be very strong demand."

The crush number added to concerns tight old crop supplies won't last through the summer. Cash sources attributed the higher number in part to improved crush margins. Margins have slipped back this week as beans surged and products faltered.

Gains were limited by USDA's weekly export sales figures which came in below expectations. USDA on Thursday pegged U.S. net export sales of U.S. 1996-97 soybeans at 145,900 tonnes, below expectations for 150,000 to 200,000 tonnes.
Soybeans ended 11 to three cents per bushel higher with July up 11 at $8.80-1/2 and new crop November up 2-1/4 at $6.84-3/4.

Several floor sources noted USDA's new crop export sales of 345,600 tonnes were more than double the old crop tally, suggesting world buyers had covered immediate needs and had enough supplies to tide them over until lower priced new crop came available in the fall.

Ideas new crop demand will be strong have supported November despite expectations for a bumper crop. Trade sources noted Brazilian sources expect Brazil's new crop imports to double to two million tonnes with up to half of that seen coming from the United States.
They pointed to the record export pace out of Brazil, noting it made economic sense for South America to ship as much as possible to take advantage of the nearby premium.
Technically, the old crop contracts continued to give off bullish signals, closing above the 50-day moving average for the second day.
Chartists put resistance at $8.82 per bushel in the July.
On the day, Griffin Trading bought three million bushels July, FIMAT Futures bought two million July and ADM bought two million July, pit sources said.

In spreads, the July/November tacked on roughly eight cents to close at $1.92-3/4 cents. Tenco Inc, FIMAT Futures, Prudential Securities, Dean Witter and SAK Futures were all said to be July/November bull spreaders.

In options trade, LFG bought 600 July $9.00 calls and sold 600 July $9.25 calls at 6-1/2 cents. Louis Dreyfus sold 300 July $9.00 calls at 13-1/2 to 12-1/2 cents and Merrill Lynch bought 400 July $8.75 calls at 27 to 28-1/2 cents.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 78,000 contracts, well below Thursday's actual volume of 107,601.
